issues.legal_issue: A bid cannot be treated as below a binding reserve price when that price was not disclosed in the invitation to bid.
material_facts: The expert committee had indicated a reserve-price figure, but the advertisement inviting bids did not disclose any reserve price.
The appellant submitted the highest bid, which was accepted; the successful bidder paid the bid amount and a sale deed was executed.
The respondent’s bid was also below the committee’s indicated figure.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred in treating the accepted bid as below a binding reserve price; the committee’s undisclosed figure did not invalidate the sale.
issues.legal_principle: A reserve-price figure not stated in the invitation to bid cannot be treated as a disclosed bidding condition. The Court relied on the terms of the advertisement and the fact that it specified no reserve price; it cited no earlier case on this issue.

predicates.tender_award_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a decision setting aside an award made through a bidding process.
predicates.no_reserve_price_disclosed: The invitation to bid did not disclose a reserve price to bidders.
predicates.highest_bid_accepted: The authority accepted the highest bid submitted in the bidding process.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a bid award, the invitation disclosed no reserve price, and the authority accepted the highest bid, the award is not invalid because of an undisclosed reserve price.

issues.legal_issue: A bidder’s failure to strictly comply with a financial-information requirement does not invalidate an outright-sale award when the requirement is ancillary to the sale’s main objective and the bidder promptly pays the bid amount.
material_facts: The advertised transaction was an outright sale, not an arrangement requiring an ongoing relationship or continued performance by the bidder.
The advertisement requested annual-turnover and net-worth information for the preceding three years.
The appellant did not provide the requested information, but submitted the highest bid, paid the entire bid amount within the prescribed period, and received a sale deed.

The authorities accepted the bid after consideration by a committee; the respondent alleged non-compliance with the information requirement but did not allege arbitrariness, bias, favoritism, or malice in the auction process.
issues.conclusion: The financial-information requirement was ancillary rather than essential, and the authorities could waive strict literal compliance; the award and sale deed remained valid.
issues.legal_principle: Under Poddar Steel Corporation v. Ganesh Engineering Works and Others, tender conditions may be distinguished between essential eligibility requirements, which may need rigid enforcement, and ancillary or subsidiary requirements, from which an authority may depart in appropriate cases. Here, because the transaction was a sale simpliciter requiring payment rather than continuing performance or a particular financial status, the information requirement was ancillary and strict compliance could be waived.

rule.if: tender_award_appeal and outright_sale and condition_only_supports_payment and no_continuing_obligations and bidder_paid_promptly

predicates.tender_award_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a decision setting aside an award made through a bidding process.
predicates.outright_sale: The transaction transfers the subject of the bid outright rather than establishing a continuing arrangement.
predicates.condition_only_supports_payment: The disputed condition serves only to support the objective of ensuring that the bidder can pay the bid amount.
predicates.no_continuing_obligations: The transaction imposes no continuing obligations requiring assurance of the bidder’s sustained financial capacity.
predicates.bidder_paid_promptly: The successful bidder paid the bid amount within the required period.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns an outright-sale award, the disputed condition only supports payment, no continuing obligations require sustained financial capacity, and the successful bidder pays promptly, the award remains valid despite non-compliance with that ancillary condition.
